Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a CXMS (Cross-linking Mass Spectrometry) study using BS3 and EDC/NHS crosslinkers to determine the conformation of MCAK. While phosphorylation is a central biological theme of the paper, the proteomics assay itself is focused on cross-link identification and quantification of cross-linked residue pairs rather than a phospho-enrichment workflow.

organism: analyzed the 3D structure of human MCAK in solution
scope: We isolated a species with a higher molecular mass of 160 kDa, corresponding to dimeric MCAK, from a denaturing gel
10 ug MCAK was mixed with 20 ug BS3
For MCAK–microtubule crosslinking, 10 ug microtubules were preactivated... 10 ug MCAK was added
Crosslinked samples (red box, Fig. 3C) were reduced, alkylated and trypsin digested

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics analysis was performed on purified recombinant human MCAK (and its mutants) and MCAK-microtubule complexes, not on whole cell lysates. Sf9 and BL21 cells were used as expression systems for protein production.

primary_biological_variables.matched_definition: Comparison between wild-type and mutant or variant alleles, proteins, or genotypes.
evidence: To compare MCAK and MCAKS6E quantitatively, a workflow that integrated the MaxQuant (v1.5.3.30) for spectra pre-processing, Xi (v1.6.743, ) for crosslinked peptide identification and Skyline (v4.1.0.11717) for MS1-based quantification was used.
We generated an Aurora B phosphomimetic MCAK mutant for six serine residues (MCAKS6E) to ensure the sample was fully modified on the residues that are phosphorylated in vivo.
